newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Nat'l Coffee Fund seeks foreign credit.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Nat'l Coffee Fund seeks foreign credit.

text.p: Colombia's National Coffee Fund will borrow up to $100 million on foreign markets before year-end to help shore up its battered finances, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said.

He said the loan would help finance the fund's growing fiscal deficit, which has widened in recent months because of low world coffee prices and the recent strengthening of Colombia's peso currency, which erodes the value of export revenues.
"We think that with this line of credit, the National Coffee Fund's situation will be more than manageable until the end of the year," Ocampo told reporters.

He spoke after an emergency meeting of the policy-making National Coffee Committee, called to discuss measures aimed at saving the Coffee Fund from possible collapse because of a predicted deficit of at least 120 billion pesos for the 1995-96 coffee year.
The fund is operated by the National Coffee Growers Federation and purchases green coffee from growers.
The National Coffee Committee had been widely expected to cut Colombia's internal coffee price during Thursday's meeting to take some financial pressure off the Coffee Fund.
But Ocampo said it had been decided to maintain the price set last August at 235,500 pesos per 125-kilogram load.
He added, however, that a premimum of 14,000 pesos per load, paid because of poor prospects for this year's harvest, would now be paid in the form of a government bond instead of cash.
The three-year bond will carry an annual interest rate of 20 percent, Ocampo said.
